text:
alice: kicking off a quick checkin on aggregation/reconciliation heuristics for tokenized provisional increments. Wanted to capture operational tradeoffs and a minimal rollout plan.

ben: TL;DR? what's the core failure mode we're trying to avoid?

alice: core issue: provisional increments (token->bucket counters) can diverge from resolved billing when canonical traces are delayed or lost. That breaks finance dashboards and causes noisy alerts. We need a bounded eventual-consistency model with clear visibility.

carla: two-part strategy: (1) aggregation design that is idempotent and dedupe-friendly; (2) reconciliation pipeline that materializes final billing keys and replays diffs into settled counters.

dan: idempotency: recommend using (token, model_bucket, delta_id) as the aggregator key. delta_id is a short opaque nonce derived from request_id+worker_id to dedupe retries. Keep delta_id size small (8-12 chars).

finance-bot: Important: settled counters must be the single source of truth for billing; provisional counts are only for near-real-time visibility.

ben: what about token collisions? If token is low-card, different requests could map to same token; how do we ensure attribution accuracy?

alice: collisions are acceptable at coarse granularity but must be bounded. We'll track token_collision_rate metric and add an alert if >0.05% for 1h. Also prefer salted hashing per-tenant to reduce cross-tenant collisions.

carla: reconciliation pipeline: when canonical trace resolves, it writes (token -> resolved_key, list of delta_ids). Reconciler joins those deltas and applies idempotent increments to final bucket, then marks provisional deltas as reconciled and emits a reverse-adjustment to provisional counters.

dan: implementation note: reconciler should be streaming but with a configurable watermark: hold unsettled tokens for W_hold (default 60m) before considering them permanently missing. That bounds storage.

alice: policy for missing tokens after W_hold: emit a 'missing_resolution' alert and route to manual investigation; but finance should get a correction window policy (e.g., we bill on reconciled keys after 24h).

ben: what about duplicates from retries? aggregator must be able to dedupe; delta_id covers that. If worker replays same delta with same delta_id, aggregator should ignore.

carla: storage model: use a time-series store for provisional increments with TTL 1h; reconciled increments apply to billing store (long-term). The reconciler writes a tombstone to provisional store on reconcile.

finance-bot: UI: console shows three series: provisional, reconciled (settled), and corrective adjustments. Provide a reconciliation-lag histogram.

alice: rollout: (1) implement aggregator with dedupe keys + metrics behind FF; (2) implement reconciler as consumer of canonical trace topic; (3) instrument dashboards and alerts; (4) canary 1% tenant traffic for 48h; (5) widen to 10% then 100%.

dan: threshold/rollback: if reconciled delta (sum|settled - provisional|) > 1% for 24h, auto-roll back tokenized ingest for impacted tenants.

carla: testing: unit tests for dedupe logic, property tests for delta_id collisions, e2e chaos: delay reconciler and verify eventual correction and that provisional counters are adjusted exactly once.

alice: privacy/security: tokens must not contain PII and must be HMAC-salted per-region. Access controls on the join table. Audit logs for reconciler operations.

ben: perf: aggregator must support high QPS; implement sharded in-memory dedupe cache with eviction tuned to delta retention.

carla: add a debug capture header we can use to force delta emission of full spans for a request (rate-limited). Helpful for troubleshooting.

obs-bot: Created ticket OBS-4222 "agg reconciliation pipeline + dedupe keys" assigned to alice,ben,carla,dan.

alice: ok I'll draft RFC appendices (sequence diagrams + example protos + sample logs) and post link. Assign follow-ups: alice+dan: proto+delta_id scheme (2d); ben+carla: reconciler/metrics+dashboards (4d); finance-bot: verify reconciliation UI requirements and reporting (3d).

ben: thanks all, this should keep provisional counts useful without surprising finance.
